Widow remarriage Act was passed in?
x:
The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856 legalized the remarriage of Hindu widows in British India. The Act was enacted largely due to the relentless efforts of the great social reformer Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, who campaigned against the social injustice faced by widows. In Andhra Pradesh, Kandukuri Veeresalingam Pantulu became the foremost champion of widow remarriage. Inspired by the Act, he organized the first widow remarriage in Andhra in 1881, despite severe opposition from orthodox sections of society. The Act marked a turning point in the history of social reforms in India by improving the legal status of Hindu widows.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).
